sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Racines, known to the municipality as Ratschings, is a mountain municipality in South Tyrol whose parking question is about reaching the Ratschings-Jaufen ski and hiking area. The written rules are thin: the municipal register shows that the council approved an ordinance regulating parking, camping and other overnight stays on 23 April 2026, but only the title is public, so we do not know its zones or fines [6]. In 2022 the executive recorded a further commitment under the commission to a Brixen engineering firm for a mobility concept as part of the municipal development programme, and we did not find the concept itself [7]. The main alternative to the car is public transport and a ski bus. The tourist office says regular buses run roughly hourly from the railway station in Sterzing, about 10 km away, to the Ratschings, Ridnaun and Jaufental valleys, and that the activeCard given by most accommodations allows free use of all public transport in South Tyrol [13]. The ski bus for winter 2025/26 was free for guests with that card and, according to its poster, ran on 5 to 8 December, 12 to 14 December and from 19 December 2025 to 12 April 2026 on three routes with one to three runs a day [12].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The register shows works on village car parks, but only award titles. In 2025 the executive awarded contracts for a new public car park in the Stange I extension zone, staking out the boundaries, construction and drainage and asphalting, and the register does not show completion or the number of spaces [10]. In December 2025 it commissioned asphalting at the public car park in Ridnaun Dorf and a new car park at the association hall in Jaufental [11]. On 20 October 2023 the council dealt with a land-use plan amendment for a roundabout in Stange, without saying whether it was an adoption or a final approval [8]. On charging, the executive approved an agreement with Plenitude on the road on 8 October 2025 for the supply, installation and management of charging infrastructure, with no locations or numbers shown [5]. The tourist office lists a public charging point in Stange next to the sports zone, with one 50 kW CCS, one 50 kW CHAdeMO and one 43 kW Type 2 connector [4].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The key site is the multi-storey car park at the valley station of the Ratschings-Jaufen cabin lift. The lift operator's page says it has about 300 spaces, is free in summer and costs 1.50 euros an hour in the winter season, with a clearance of 2.20 metres; this is the only published tariff we found, and the page is undated [1]. The page does not state who runs the car park, but it is presented on the lift company's website, which suggests the company does [2]. It lists three charging stations on the first floor, two of 22 kW and one of 7.4 kW [3]. The South Tyrol Open Data Hub records two lift car parks, zone 1 with 222 spaces and zone 2 with 60, 282 together, which does not match the 300 on the operator's page, and it marks both as having no charging [0]. The summer cable-car season began on 30 May 2026, and the winter season is announced for 4 December 2026 to 4 April 2027 [14][15].

Our data cover both zones since 27 September 2026, 24 days for zone 1 and 15 for zone 2, which is outside the winter season. Zone 1 averaged about 24% on both weekdays and weekends, with a peak of 42% on a Sunday afternoon. Zone 2 averaged 2% on weekdays and 4% at weekends and peaked at 28% on a Sunday morning. These are autumn figures, and winter figures will differ.
